description: Live thermal wander on cavity 01: one slow cooling-water driver moves body temperature, reflected power, forward power and tuner position together, each with its own readback noise, so a live correlation plot of temperature against reflected power (or tuner) shows a noisy, elongated cloud whose strength drifts over tens of seconds. For correlation demos; it adds no archived excursions (use rf-thermal for those) and does not compose with rf-thermal, which touches the same channels.
_comment: `cav01-thermal` is a wander stack (5 log-spaced sines) with slowest period 300 s, so its
Gains are in channel units per unit driver: +-0.5 degC body temperature, +-0.08 cm tuner,
+-2.5 kW reflected and forward power. Reflected power's gain rides a slow envelope
(x0.2..x1.8, slowest period 900 s), so its correlation with temperature waxes and wanes:
sampled at 1 s, r(T, REV) over a 5-min window wanders ~0.5-0.87; r(T, TUNER) ~0.96-0.98;
r(T, FWD) ~0.85-0.9. The `noise` block replaces these channels' machine-file noise while
the scenario is active (relative noise off, absolute sigma set) so the readback noise is
independent per channel and sized for those correlations. Couplings are deterministic in
epoch time, so archived history shows the same wander as the live values.
